scenes.headline: the IDE, wired in
scenes.illustrates: The poster frame names the project (eyebrow oh-my-pi) above the one-line thesis, so a muted viewer sees the name and the claim, the IDE is wired in, in the first second.
Inside a live editor window one symbol is renamed and the imports update on their own, showing that omp routes the edit through the language server instead of find-and-replacing text.
Two panes side by side make the contrast literal, the crowd printing values to guess while omp attaches real debuggers, so the split itself is the argument.

lines: edits anchor to a content hash
scenes.illustrates: The words name the mechanism the rename just enacted, a content-hash anchor rather than a line number, so the picture and the sentence reinforce the same idea.

scenes.title: one kernel cell
scenes.illustrates: The peak shows spawned code reaching back into the agent's own tools, python reading a file with tool.read and javascript charting it in one cell, the one move no other coding agent shows.

scenes.caption: stars and climbing
scenes.illustrates: After the mechanics earned it, the count lands the scale of adoption in one near-black numeral so the receipt reads without a chart.

scenes.subtitle: built by a reverse engineer
scenes.illustrates: The close credits the builder and returns to the wordmark, rhyming with the opening frame so the autoloop seam reads clean.
